config.grain_rationale: Each record is a legal entity (identified by ABN) with its tax information for an income year. The business participant's legal name and ABN are mapped; the financial figures are outside the ontology.

record_id.rationale: Neither Name (526 distinct/527) nor ABN (524 distinct/527, 2 missing) is unique per record, so a content hash is the traceable record id.

fields.rationale: The ATO corporate tax transparency report lists entities by their registered legal name; names carry legal-form suffixes (PTY LTD, PTY LIMITED, LIMITED).
ABN column is 11 digits and 100% checksum-valid across the discovery partition; 2 records legitimately have no ABN.

config.notes:
Mapped the main data sheet 'Income tax details'. The 'Information' sheet is front-matter with no tabular records; the 'PRRT details' sheet (16 records: Name, ABN, PRRT Payable $) is a separate supplementary table not covered by this config. Restricting to one sheet keeps one row = one legal entity; no publisher documentation was supplied, so semantics rest on the sheet headers and the report's published structure.

[ext-v1] The core ontology previously discarded the three financial columns as out-of-scope; the extension registry now has ext.financial.* targets, so total income, taxable income and tax payable map as period facts with period = Income year and currency AUD. Taxable income and tax payable are only 76%/72% populated - blanks stay missing, never zero. Name carries no registrar legal-form code (no ASIC type/class column exists in this file), so no legal_form or legal_form_detail claim is made; inferring a legal form from 'PTY LTD' in the name would be an inference the source does not state. No licence, establishment, contact or address data is present, so no extra record roles or relationships are declared. Note the file's 'Income year' also contains 9 rows of 2022-23 in the 2023-24 release; those rows' financial facts carry 2022-23 as the period rather than being dropped.
